source.title: Towards an Improved Understanding and Utilization of Maximum Manifold Capacity Representations
source.authors: Rylan Schaeffer; Victor Lecomte; Dhruv B. Pai; Andres Carranza; Berivan Isik; A. Unell; Mikail Khona; Thomas E. Yerxa; Yann LeCun; SueYeon Chung; Andrey Gromov; Ravid Shwartz-Ziv; O. Koyejo

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent as an analogy, but its experiments measure MMCR pretraining percent error and multimodal zero-shot accuracy, not test error over model size, epochs, or sample size as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a double-descent-like pattern in MMCR pretraining percent error versus number of manifolds P and embedding dimension D. This is a different measure from the test error named in the versions, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. The multimodal batch-size results concern zero-shot accuracy and do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The double-descent-like result concerns MMCR pretraining percent error (a training-loss gap to a bound) versus batch size P and embedding dimension D. It is not test error over model size, epochs or sample count. The zero-shot batch-size sweep also does not measure any version's quantity, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors predict theoretically, and confirm empirically, a double-descent-like peak in MMCR pretraining percent error at P=D, with respect to atypical hyperparameters. They also report compute scaling laws for that error and show MMCR matches CLIP at small batch sizes but lags at larger ones. They do not report test-error double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes MMCR pretraining percent error across manifolds and embedding dimensions; it does not reproduce the original test-error experiments across model size, epochs, or sample size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported pretraining percent-error pattern is examined across P, D, and K; the text states it appears for all tested K combinations. Multimodal zero-shot accuracy varies with batch size, but that result does not test a listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: MMCR pretraining percent error peaks at P=D and falls on either side, for all K in {2,4,8} (Fig. 3). At P=D the compute scaling curves start higher and fall more slowly (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For MMCR-pretrained ResNet-18 on STL-10, the pretraining percent error is non-monotonic in batch size P and embedding dimension D, peaking at P=D.

fits_no_version.finding: Multimodal MMCR ImageNet zero-shot accuracy is non-monotonic in batch size at D=1024. It is best at 128–256 and poorest at the smallest batches or batches near 1024 (Fig. 5, Fig. 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal MMCR downstream accuracy degrades when batch size approaches the embedding dimension.

record.problems: The reported P-by-D result is presented graphically without numerical values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are stated for it. The measured outcome is pretraining percent error rather than test error.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the paper's multimodal batch-size sweep reports zero-shot ImageNet accuracy, not a measure named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Test error vs model size; no model-size sweep.
Test error over epochs; the compute curves (Fig. 4) are pretraining error, monotone power laws.
Test error vs number of training samples.
Risk across model classes past interpolation.
No effective-complexity measure of peak location.

missing.what: Zero-shot ImageNet accuracy vs batch size for multimodal MMCR, worst near batch size = D = 1024. This is a downstream-performance analogue of the P=D peak; no row records it.

record.verdict_notes: The theory (Theorem 3.5) explains the peak via the nuclear-norm bound of random matrices, so the analogy to classical double descent is structural, not a test of generalization. The study cites both originals only as background.

versions.untested_parts: Test error over model size and its peak near the training-set interpolation threshold.
Test error as training sample size increases near the interpolation threshold.
Generalization risk across model classes as capacity passes the interpolation point.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
Effects of label noise, variance, multiple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization on the claimed test-error peak.
Whether counting effective parameters converts the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Swept number of data points P and embedding dimension D and measured MMCR pretraining percent error.
rows.note: The text states that for all tested K combinations the pretraining percent error peaked at P = D and declined on either side. The plotted values are not transcribed here; this measure is not test error, so it cannot establish a listed claim version.
rows.check: Link to none is correct: the measure is pretraining percent error (training objective), not test error. P is the batch size or number of manifolds, not training sample count. The study states the peak sits at P=D for all K, but values are figure-only (Fig. 3).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
